name: Superconducting transmon qubit characterization in a dilution refrigerator

sources.citation: Tuokkola, M., Sunada, Y., Kivijärvi, H., Albanese, J., Grönberg, L., Kaikkonen, J.-P., Vesterinen, V., Govenius, J., Möttönen, M. (2025). Methods to achieve near-millisecond energy relaxation and dephasing times for a superconducting transmon qubit. Nature Communications 16, 5421.

Place, A. P. M., Rodgers, L. V. H., Mundada, P., Smitham, B. M., Fitzpatrick, M., Leng, Z., Premkumar, A., Bryon, J., Vrajitoarea, A., Sussman, S., Cheng, G., Madhavan, T., Babla, H. K., Le, X. H., Gang, Y., Jäck, B., Gyenis, A., Yao, N., Cava, R. J., de Leon, N. P., Houck, A. A. (2021). New material platform for superconducting transmon qubits with coherence times exceeding 0.3 milliseconds. Nature Communications 12, 1779.

reported_conditions.as_printed: Amumetal magnetic shield inside the OVC
rf attenuators, Eccosorb infrared filter, low-pass filter
attenuated on each plate; Eccosorb CR110

requirements.rationale: Tuokkola et al. (2025) operate at ~10 mK and Place et al. (2021) at a ~9–20 mK base; 20 mK is the upper end of what these papers used. Neither source states a minimum temperature as a physical necessity, so this is the papers' operating range confirmed by the user.

Observed frequencies in the sources reach 6.23 GHz (Tuokkola et al. readout resonators) and 7.3 GHz (Place et al. readout resonators); the 8 GHz figure adds margin above these and is the profile author's choice (user_entered), see reported_conditions for the observed values.

Both papers enclose the sample in high-permeability magnetic shielding (Amumetal shield and QCage shielding in Tuokkola et al.; mu-metal can in Place et al., stated to reduce ambient-field penetration during the superconducting transition). User confirms shielding is required.

Neither paper states the number of coaxial lines. At least one input (drive/readout) and one output (readout) line are implied by the described signal path, so 2 is an inferred lower bound. Non-mandatory.
Place et al. (2021) dice chips into 7 × 7 mm squares; the sample holder must accept a 7 mm wide chip. Chip size is this paper's design choice, confirmed by the user.
Place et al. (2021) dice chips into 7 × 7 mm squares; the sample holder must accept a 7 mm long chip. This paper's design choice, confirmed by the user.

missing_information: number of coaxial lines not stated in either paper
per-stage attenuation values and total attenuation not stated in the main texts
final chip size not stated by Tuokkola et al. (only 25 mm × 30 mm fabrication coupons)
dilution refrigerator make/model not stated by Place et al.; Tuokkola et al. main text says 'Bluefors' (model XLD400sl appears only in the arXiv v3 table)
thermal load / cooling power at base not stated
confirmation_note: Requirements reviewed and confirmed by the profile author on 2026-10-31 against the quoted evidence records. Any edited value must be re-confirmed by the user before the profile is used.
